newsitem.title: POLAND: ADMINISTRATIVE REFORM DIVIDES POLISH COALITION.
newsitem.headline: ADMINISTRATIVE REFORM DIVIDES POLISH COALITION.

text.p: The Peasant Party on Thursday warned its government partner, the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), it might quit the coalition if SLD goes ahead with a plan to radically reform Poland's administrative system.

The Peasants, which have made several such threats during the three years of the coalition's uneasy existence, said they were against the reform, which would introduce a new mid-level administrative unit, called Powiat, ran by locally elected governments.

"If we continue to observe enforcing the idea of Powiat, then we will not see a possibility of participating in the coalition and this will not be our fault," Peasants' senior official and Senate's speaker Adam Struzik said.
Struzik told a news conference that his party was concerned that the Alliance was seeking a support for the scheme from the biggest opposition party, the Union for Freedom.

Analysts say the Peasant Party is against the reform, which would also enlarge the current provinces and cut their number, because it could lose some of its strong influence in the current local authorities.
It proposes maintaining the current 49 provinces but put local governments in charge of them rather let them be controlled by centrally appointed governors. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
